The [Nobel Prize in Physics](Nobel_Prize_in_Physics "Nobel Prize in Physics") ([Swedish](Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Nobelpriset i fysik*) is awarded annually by the [Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences](Royal_Swedish_Academy_of_Sciences "Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences") to scientists in the various fields of [physics](Physics "Physics"). It is one of the five [Nobel Prizes](Nobel_Prize "Nobel Prize") established by the 1895 [will](Will_and_testament "Will and testament") of [Alfred Nobel](Alfred_Nobel "Alfred Nobel") (who died in 1896), awarded for outstanding contributions in physics.[[1]](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics#cite_note-1) As dictated by Nobel's will, the award is administered by the [Nobel Foundation](Nobel_Foundation "Nobel Foundation") and awarded by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.[[2]](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics#cite_note-2) The award is presented in <Stockholm> at an annual ceremony on 10 December, the anniversary of Nobel's death.[[3]](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics#cite_note-3) Each recipient receives a medal, a diploma and a monetary award prize that has varied throughout the years.[[4]](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics#cite_note-4)

The Nobel Prize in Physics has been awarded to 221 individuals until 2022.[[5]](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics#cite_note-5) The first prize in physics was awarded in 1901 to [Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen](Wilhelm_R%C3%B6ntgen "Wilhelm Röntgen"), of Germany, who received 150,782 [SEK](Swedish_krona "Swedish krona"). [John Bardeen](John_Bardeen "John Bardeen") is the only laureate to win the prize twice—in 1956 and 1972. [Marie Skłodowska-Curie](Marie_Sk%C5%82odowska-Curie "Marie Skłodowska-Curie") also won two Nobel Prizes, for physics in 1903 and chemistry in 1911.

[William Lawrence Bragg](Lawrence_Bragg "Lawrence Bragg") was the youngest Nobel laureate in physics; he won the prize in 1915 at the age of 25. He was also the youngest laureate for any Nobel prize until 2014 (when [Malala Yousafzai](Malala_Yousafzai "Malala Yousafzai") won the Nobel Peace Prize at age 17).[[6]](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics#cite_note-6) The oldest Nobel Prize laureate in physics was [Arthur Ashkin](Arthur_Ashkin "Arthur Ashkin") who was 96 years old when he was awarded the prize in 2018.[[7]](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics#cite_note-7)
